newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Thursday on profit-taking from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 3,286 yuan ($396) per tonne, losing two yuan. It opened at 3,286 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,288 and a low of 3,283.
July rose six yuan to 3,260, September fell two to 3,284, the January 1998 seven to 3,298 and March one to 3,299.
Combined volume rose to 20,000 tonnes from 15,800.
Soybeans opened little changed and fell steadily for most of the session, traders said.
"Profit-taking from retail investors dominated today's trading and the market seems unattractive to most institutions due to its long-standing weak performance," one trader said.
"The booming stock market today sucked large amounts of hot money from the futures market," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around the 3,300-yuan level early next week due to a lack of market-moving news.
